headline: Federal aid cuts pressure revenue as guidance moves higher
summary_short: Revenue fell 4.5% y/y to $1.31 billion as USAID/DOS program cancellations hit the Government Services segment, while diluted EPS eased to $0.42 from $0.43; backlog rose to $4.49 billion and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.56-$1.59.
summary_long: Third-quarter revenue fell 4.5% y/y to $1.31 billion (net revenue $1.11 billion) as USAID/DOS terminations and lower disaster-response work cut the Government Services segment, partly offset by 7.7% growth in Commercial/International on UK water demand. Gross margin ticked up to 18.6% from 18.4%. Operating income fell 4.2% to $157.9 million; diluted EPS eased to $0.42 from $0.43 on a smaller share count. Cash rose to $230.8 million on a record $467 million of nine-month operating cash flow, while long-term debt fell 9.0% q/q on debt paydown. Backlog reached $4.49 billion, up 5% sequentially, and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.56-$1.59 and narrowed net-revenue guidance to $4.315-$4.365 billion.

drivers.explanation: USAID/DOS contract cancellations and lower disaster-response activity cut Government Services revenue; Commercial/International growth from UK water demand partly offset. Backlog rose and management raised FY26 guidance on YTD performance.
GSG segment revenue fell 15.6% on USAID/DOS program cancellations and lower disaster-response work; CIG segment revenue grew 7.7% on UK water and digital-water project demand, partially offsetting.
Net revenue fell y/y on the same USAID/DOS and disaster-response declines, though management states it rose 8% y/y excluding those two items.
Gross margin expanded to 18.6% from 18.4% y/y as cost of revenue fell slightly faster than revenue itself; the release gives no standalone gross-margin explanation.
GSG operating income fell with its revenue decline; CIG operating income rose 9.7% on higher net revenue, without fully offsetting GSG's drop.
Pretax income tracked the operating-income decline; net interest expense also fell 13.6% y/y on lower borrowings and average debt interest rates.
Diluted EPS fell to $0.42 from $0.43 on lower pretax income, partly cushioned by a smaller diluted share count (259.8M vs 264.9M) from buybacks.
Cash rose sequentially on a record $467 million of nine-month operating cash flow, which funded acquisitions, buybacks, and dividends while still growing the balance.
Long-term debt fell q/q as the company used cash flow to pay down term-loan and revolver borrowings under its Amended Credit Agreement.
Equity dipped slightly q/q as $100 million of Q3 share buybacks and dividends paid out slightly outpaced net income added to retained earnings.
